title: New Job? Your First Payslip Could Be Almost £210 Short 😱🧾 #shorts
description:
New job? Your first payslip could be almost £210 short, because of the code next to your name.

1257L is the code for most people with one job and no untaxed income or taxable benefits, and the emergency code for all employees in 2026/27. It isn't a reference number: 1257 is your £12,570 tax-free Personal Allowance with the last digit dropped, and L means you get the standard allowance. Start a new job without a P45 and your employer may use 0T (or BR) instead: none of your pay from that job is tax-free. On £2,500 in your first month, 1257L takes £290.50 in tax; 0T takes £500. That's £209.50 more (almost £210), the same as one month of the allowance (£12,570 ÷ 12 × 20%).

The part most people miss: it isn't lost. Once HMRC has your details (a P45 helps) it updates your code, usually within 35 days of you starting, and your employer refunds the overpaid tax through your pay. If your old employer never confirms you've left, HMRC sorts it out after the tax year ends.

Sources: https://www.gov.uk/tax-codes/what-your-tax-code-means · https://www.gov.uk/employee-tax-codes · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/p9x-tax-codes/p9x-tax-codes-to-use-from-6-april-2026 · https://www.gov.uk/guidance/changes-to-your-tax-code-when-you-start-a-new-job · https://www.gov.uk/tax-codes/if-youve-paid-too-much-or-too-little-tax · https://www.gov.uk/tax-codes/emergency-tax-codes · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/rates-and-allowances-income-tax/income-tax-rates-and-allowances-current-and-past

Official: without a P45 or starter checklist a new employer may give a BR or 0T code; a P45 helps HMRC get your details
Official: 0T = Personal Allowance used up, or a new job where the employer lacks the details to give a code: no tax-free pay from that job
Official: HMRC usually updates your tax code within 35 days of you starting a new job
